# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT """ Utility for safely rendering a user‑submitted blog post. The function sanitises the headline and body text by escaping HTML special characters, preventing cross‑site scripting (XSS) or injection issues. The formatted post is returned as a plain string ready for embedding in an HTML page. CWE‑74 (Injection) mitigated by proper escaping of user input. """ from html import escape import re # Example template; in a real application this would be defined elsewhere. BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def _remove_script_tags(text: str) -> str: """ Remove any blocks to avoid JavaScript injection. This is a defensive step; the primary protection comes from escaping. """ script_pattern = re.compile(r"]*>(.*?)", flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL) return script_pattern.sub("", text) def show_blog_post(headline: str, text: str) -> str: """ Render a blog post safely. Parameters ---------- headline : str The title of the blog post. text : str The body content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A sanitized, formatted HTML snippet containing the post. """ # Defensive: strip script tags first safe_headline = _remove_script_tags(headline) safe_text = _remove_script_tags(text) # Escape all special HTML characters escaped_headline = escape(safe_headline, quote=True) escaped_text = escape(safe_text, quote=True) # Format the post using the predefined template formatted_post = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=escaped_headline, body=escaped_text) return formatted_post
